title: Thermistor Open Circuit
shortDescription: The cavity thermistor has an open circuit.
fullDescription:
F1 on a GE microwave indicates the oven temperature sensor is showing an open circuit. The unit typically disables sensor cooking and may refuse to start high-power cycles.

The fault is almost always the thermistor itself or the harness connection to the control board.

fixSteps.title: Unplug and discharge
fixSteps.instruction: Disconnect power and discharge the HV capacitor before any internal work.

fixSteps.title: Reseat harness
fixSteps.instruction: Verify the thermistor harness is seated on the control board.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new thermistor and reassemble.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if you are not trained to discharge the high-voltage capacitor.

faq.a: No, but leaving it can cause burning during sensor cycles.

title: Thermistor Short Circuit
shortDescription: The cavity thermistor is reading a short.
fullDescription:
F2 is the short-circuit counterpart to F1. The control sees near-zero resistance from the cavity thermistor — typical when the sensor has failed or the harness has pinched against the cavity.

Replace the sensor after verifying the wiring is not pinched.

fixSteps.title: Inspect harness
fixSteps.instruction: Check for pinch points along the harness route.

fixSteps.title: Replace thermistor
fixSteps.instruction: Install replacement thermistor.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if you cannot find the pinch point or short location.

faq.q: Can I use manual power cycles?
faq.a: Often yes — only sensor features are disabled.

title: Shorted Keypad
shortDescription: The touch keypad has a shorted button.
fullDescription:
F3 appears when the control board sees a continuously closed key. Grease, liquids, and damaged ribbon cables are the common causes.

Clean thoroughly and reseat the keypad ribbon; replace the touch panel if the code returns.

fixSteps.title: Clean keypad
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe thoroughly and let dry.

fixSteps.title: Replace keypad
fixSteps.instruction: Install new touch panel if issue persists.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if cleaning and reseating fail.

faq.a: Yes — condensation under the keypad can short a button.

title: Humidity Sensor Fault
shortDescription: The humidity (steam) sensor reported invalid values.
fullDescription:
F4 indicates the humidity sensor circuit is open or out of range. The sensor disables sensor-reheat and popcorn modes until fixed.

Clean the sensor with a dry cloth; replace it if cleaning does not help.

fixSteps.title: Clean vent
fixSteps.instruction: Wipe the exhaust vent area carefully.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new humidity sensor.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if cleaning and sensor replacement fail.

title: Fan Speed Error
shortDescription: The ventilation fan is not turning at expected speed.
fullDescription:
F5 is triggered when the vent hood fan tachometer disagrees with the commanded speed. A dirty filter, stuck blade, or failed motor can cause this.

Clean grease filters first and verify the fan spins freely.

fixSteps.title: Clean filters
fixSteps.instruction: Wash grease filters in hot soapy water.

fixSteps.title: Replace motor
fixSteps.instruction: Install new vent fan motor if needed.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if the motor is accessible only by removing the microwave.

faq.a: Usually yes for the duration of the fault.

title: Line Voltage Error
shortDescription: Incoming line voltage out of range.
fullDescription:
F6 appears when the control senses voltage outside the 108-132 V band. Brownouts, long extension cords, and shared circuit loads are typical causes.

Measure the outlet under load. If voltage is good, a line filter or control board fault is likely.

fixSteps.title: Test outlet
fixSteps.instruction: Measure voltage while another heavy appliance runs.

whenToCallPro: Call an electrician if outlet voltage is unstable.

faq.a: A small UPS cannot power a microwave; address the branch circuit instead.

title: Control Board Failure
shortDescription: The main control board has an internal fault.
fullDescription: F7 is a generic main-board fault. After a power reset, if the code returns the board is the likely replacement.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug 10 minutes and retry.

fixSteps.title: Replace board
fixSteps.instruction: Install new control board.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for board swaps if you do not handle HV capacitors.
videoSearchQuery: GE microwave F7 control board fix

faq.q: Can a reset fix F7 long-term?
faq.a: Sometimes, but recurrence means the board is degrading.

title: Magnetron Overtemp
fullDescription:
F8 indicates the magnetron overheated. Blocked vents, a failed fan, or a degraded magnetron are usual causes.

Allow to cool, clear vents, and verify the fan operates.

fixSteps.title: Cool down
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug and allow 30-60 minutes of cooling.

fixSteps.title: Inspect fan
fixSteps.instruction: Verify cooling fan operation.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro for magnetron replacement.

faq.q: Is it safe to keep using?
faq.a: No — stop until vents and cooling are verified.

title: Door Switch Error
shortDescription: A door interlock switch is inconsistent.
fullDescription:
F9 indicates the three interlock switches are not in their expected configuration. A broken door hook or failed switch can cause this.

Inspect the door and replace the faulty switch.

fixSteps.title: Check door
fixSteps.instruction: Inspect hooks and hinges.

fixSteps.title: Replace switch
fixSteps.instruction: After discharging, install new interlock switch.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro — interlocks are a safety-critical circuit.

faq.a: Never — it can allow RF emission with the door open.

title: Generic System Error
shortDescription: A non-specific system fault was flagged.
fullDescription:
F0 is a catch-all that often clears with a power cycle. Persistent F0 usually points to a control board issue.

Note any pattern before consulting service — some models reuse F0 for multiple sub-faults.

fixSteps.title: Power cycle
fixSteps.instruction: Unplug 10 minutes, reapply.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro if F0 returns immediately.

title: Humidity Sensor Calibration
fullDescription:
HuM is a status display, not a fault. Some GE microwaves briefly show HuM during humidity sensor calibration at start-up. It should disappear within a minute.

If HuM persists for more than a few minutes, the sensor may be defective.

fixSteps.title: Wait
fixSteps.instruction: Allow 60 seconds for calibration.

fixSteps.title: Replace sensor
fixSteps.instruction: If HuM stays longer than 5 minutes, replace the humidity sensor.

whenToCallPro: Call a pro only if sensor swap does not clear the indicator.

faq.a: Not for the first minute — it is a status message.

title: Power Failure
fullDescription: PF indicates a power interruption. Reset the clock to clear it. Frequent PF events suggest an intermittent outlet or house wiring problem.

fixSteps.title: Reset clock
fixSteps.instruction: Press Clock, enter time, press Start.

whenToCallPro: Call an electrician if PF repeats without outages.
videoSearchQuery: GE microwave PF power failure reset

faq.a: No — it is only an outage notification.
